Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

=== .docs/prd/returns.md (full) ===
# PRD – Returns & Refunds

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheet "Returns and Refunds" (RRC). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Non-Returnable Products (RRC-001 – RRC-003, confirmed)

- Products can be marked non-returnable at SKU level; categories can be bulk-marked with SKU taking precedence (RRC-001)
- Items ineligible for return: gift cards (physical and virtual); final sale items (clearly flagged). Returnable status does not flip during sales/seasonal campaigns (RRC-001)
- **Non-returnable message** displayed in cart, mini-cart, and checkout — copy is configurable (RRC-002)
- **Non-returnable / final sale indicator** displayed on PDP (RRC-003) — see [pdp.md](pdp.md)

---

## 2. Returns Initiation (RRC-004 – RRC-005, RRC-031, confirmed)

- Returns link shown on order detail in My Account (RRC-004)
- **Domestic** (AU, US, UK, HK) → **redirect** to the **Narvar** returns portal. Returns processing is owned entirely by Narvar; there is no PWA/SFCC build beyond the redirect link (RRC-004; Third-Party Integrations, Returns/Narvar row)
- **International** → **redirect** to the **Global-e** returns portal (RRC-004; Third-Party Integrations, Returns/Global-E row)
- Both registered and guest customers use the same initiation flow: billing email + order number (RRC-005). Identity verification is managed by Narvar and Global-e respectively — no PWA-side verification logic required
- Returns policy link in checkout terms copy opens `/returns` in a new tab (RRC-031)

---

## 3. Returns Page in My Account (RRC-007 – RRC-011, RRC-014, confirmed)

- Dedicated Returns page in My Account showing completed returns only (no in-progress) (RRC-009)
- List view per return: total refund amount, original order ID, return completed date (RRC-010)
- Return Detail page per return (RRC-011)
- **Return history** sourced by calling the MuleSoft `/api/returns` experience API (`GET /api/returns?customer_id=`), which consolidates return data from NewStore OMS (RRC-007)
- **Return status** displayed on the Return History and Return Detail pages, as returned from NewStore via MuleSoft (RRC-008); status retrieved on page load for each return on the Returns page (RRC-014)
- The PWA is a **display surface only** over the MuleSoft `/api/returns` data — per 25.05 comment, "SFCC will only display what returns status is provided by MuleSoft." No PWA-side status derivation or mapping (RRC-007/008/014)
- *Open: Return Detail page must accommodate different taxes/duties per country (RRC-030) — see Open Items*

---

## 4. Cancellation & Order Status (RRC-012 – RRC-018, confirmed)

- Cancelled orders display a distinct **"Cancelled"** status label on Order History page, separate from Returned (RRC-012)
- Cancellation status surfaced on order detail page in My Account once updated by the OMS via MuleSoft (RRC-016)
- BOPIS cancellation status displayed in My Account once cancelled by the OMS (RRC-017)
- Partially cancelled orders (full, individual line item, or partial line item) surfaced in Order History and Order Detail, as returned from NewStore via MuleSoft (RRC-018)
- Order status sourced from NewStore OMS via MuleSoft Experience API (`GET /api/orders?customer_id=`), fetched at page load (RRC-013)
- Refund status: the system does not display refund status directly (RRC-015). A "refund processed" message is acceptable provided it includes a bank processing time caveat — copy managed in Contentful

---

## 5. Fraud-Flagged Orders (PAY-047 – PAY-051, ready for sign off)

- **No customer-facing communication** while an order is on fraud hold — do not build a fraud hold status display
- No auto-cancellation; no fixed maximum hold duration
- When fraud hold is cleared: NewStore releases the order → SFCC updates order status (customer sees standard "Processing" or equivalent)
- When fraud is rejected: NewStore cancels → Adyen refunds → SFCC updates status to cancelled. Customer sees "Cancelled" per section 4 above

---

## 6. Open Items

- Returns-link display/eligibility logic (ENH-014, Under Review — to be sized) — intended logic per Zimm Response (not yet confirmed): (1) display the link only if the order contains returnable items, determined via the product's returnable attribute; (2) returns window of 15 days from the delivery completion date, falling back to 28 days from order creation date where no delivery completion date is available. Rule (2) is third-party dependent — the delivery completion date must be passed back via MuleSoft. Pending sizing and the delivery-date being supplied via MuleSoft
- Return Detail page tax/duties display per country (RRC-030, Confirmed but challenged) — per 25.05 comment: "Do we display tax/duties level in My Account, or is this purely Narvar/Global-E?" (To Review: Shweta — API check). Values returned from NewStore via MuleSoft
- Return action visibility window: within 15 days of delivery vs. shipment date — TBC (CRM-066–068)

---

*Note: Manual Orders / OOBO requirements (RRC-019 – RRC-029) have been removed from PWA scope — recommendation is to keep these in Adyen. Pending scope discussion before any storefront-side work is considered.*

```
..._routes.filter((route: { path?: string }) => !EXCLUDED_BASE_ROUTES.includes(route.path ?? ''))
```

## 3. Order data available client-side

### Hooks
- **Order history** — `order-history.jsx:26,92-97`: `useCustomerOrders` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, `parameters: {customerId, limit, offset, expand: 'oms'}`, gated `{enabled: onClient && !!customerId}`.
- **Order detail** — `order-detail.jsx:26,124-134`: `useOrder`, `parameters: {orderNo: params.orderNo, expand: 'oms, oms_shipments'}`.

Both already request the **OMS expansion** — important, because OMS is where the delivery date lives.

### Actual property accesses in base code
`order-history.jsx`:
```
order.creationDate        // :151  formatDate(new Date(order.creationDate), …)
order.orderNo             // :143 key, :162 link target, :181 display
order.status || order.omsData?.status   // :185
order.productItems        // :190, :210
order.currency / order.orderTotal       // :216-217
order.shipments[0].shippingAddress.{firstName,lastName,fullName}  // :226-230
```
`order-detail.jsx`:
```
order.creationDate        // :303
order.orderNo             // :316
order.status || order.omsData?.status   // :320
order?.omsData            // :138  isOmsOrder
order?.omsData?.shipments?.length       // :140
order?.shipments?.length                // :141
shipment.shippingStatus                 // :414  omsShipment?.status || shipment.shippingStatus
shipment.trackingNumber / omsShipment?.trackingUrl  // :416-417
omsShipment?.provider                   // :412

```
**`customerInfo.email` is NOT accessed** by either page (it exists on the type — see below).

### ShopperOrders `Order` type — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:55426` (identical at `index.cjs.d.ts:55426`)

> Note: the package has **no `dist/`** directory — types live in `lib/index.{esm,cjs}.d.ts`.

**Date-ish fields (only two):**
- `creationDate?: string`
- `lastModified?: string`

**Status-ish fields:**
- `status?: OrderStatusEnum` = `"created" | "new" | "completed" | "cancelled" | "replaced" | "failed"`
- `shippingStatus?: OrderShippingStatusEnum` = `"not_shipped" | "part_shipped" | "shipped"`
- `confirmationStatus?: OrderConfirmationStatusEnum` = `"not_confirmed" | "confirmed"`
- `paymentStatus?: OrderPaymentStatusEnum` = `"not_paid" | "part_paid" | "paid"`
- `exportStatus?: OrderExportStatusEnum` = `"not_exported" | "exported" | "ready" | "failed"`
- `externalOrderStatus?: string`

**Also present:** `orderNo`, `orderToken`, `orderViewCode`, `customerInfo?: CustomerInfo`, `sourceCode?: string`, `shipments?: Array<Shipment>`, `omsData?: OmsData`, `siteId`, `guest`, plus an index signature `& {[key: string]: any}` (so `c_*` passes through untyped).

`CustomerInfo` (`:54642`): `{customerId?, customerName?, customerNo?, email: string}` — **`customerInfo.email` is available and non-optional.**

### Delivery / fulfilment completion date — the decisive answer

**The plain ECOM `Order` does NOT have one.** `Shipment` (`:54583`) has **no date fields at all**: `shipmentId, shipmentNo, shippingAddress, shippingMethod, shippingStatus, trackingNumber`, totals/tax only.

**But `OmsShipment` DOES** (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:33330`):
```ts
type OmsShipment = {
    id?: string;
    status?: string;
    provider?: string;
    trackingNumber?: string;
    trackingUrl?: string;
    expectedDeliveryDate?: string;   // Expected delivery date and time
    actualDeliveryDate?: string;     // Actual delivery date and time (null if not yet delivered)
    shipmentItems?: Array<OmsShipmentItem>;
};
type OmsData = { status?: string; shipments?: Array<OmsShipment>; };
```
**`order.omsData.shipments[n].actualDeliveryDate` is the delivery-completion date**, and base order-detail **already requests it** via `expand: 'oms, oms_shipments'` (`order-detail.jsx:128`) — it just never reads it. Order-history only sends `expand: 'oms'`, so it gets `omsData.status` but **not** shipments.

**Inferred (flag to the team):** this satisfies the ENH-014 "15 days from delivery completion date, else 28 days from creationDate" rule **without** a MuleSoft call — *provided* NewStore actually populates `actualDeliveryDate` through SFCC OMS ingestion. `.docs/prd/returns.md` assumes a MuleSoft dependency; the SDK contract suggests a cheaper path is at least worth validating on SIT.
